content.title: After creating a submission in the same browser session, the My Submissions count matches the submissions list
content.intent: Prove that the shared header reflects the current browser session's submission total after a real submission is created.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: equivalence partitioning + state / flow. I used the representative state transition from no known submission to one newly created submission in the same browser session because the source only grounds that the header count matches the current session's stored submissions. No covering array was needed because there is no independent multi-input interaction to combine for this journey; the risk-judged default strength would be 2 (no money/auth/data-loss factors apply).

content.title: Traverse the shared header navigation between home, publishing, books, and success stories
content.intent: Prove that the logo and the three primary navigation links let a visitor move between the site's major sections while the shared frame remains present on each reached page.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: equivalence partitioning + state / flow. I used one representative cross-section traversal through the shared header controls because the use-case promise is reachability between platform sections, and the route values change page destinations rather than forming a combinatorial input matrix. No covering array was needed because there are no independent input dimensions to combine; the risk-judged default strength would be 2 (no money/auth/data-loss factors apply).

content.title: Open the support page from the shared footer
content.intent: Prove that the common footer keeps support reachable from another site section through the `Contact & support` link.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: equivalence partitioning. I used a representative non-home starting section and the single grounded footer route to `/contact`, whose destination is identified by the headed `Contact & support` page in the source. No covering array was needed because this journey has one route choice and no independent interacting inputs; the risk-judged default strength would be 2 (no money/auth/data-loss factors apply).

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Highest value because it covers the only browser-session-dependent shared-frame behavior and uses a live state change that can easily drift from the UI.
[value_score] Second-highest value because it covers the logo and all primary header routes that keep the site's main sections reachable.
[value_score] Third-highest value because support reachability matters, but it is narrower than the header-wide traversal and is directly grounded by a single footer route promise.
